assertions: Essex will take Reading: the town will fall into the besieging Parliament army's hands in this siege
The town will be delivered by surrender/composition on terms rather than held successfully by the garrison, and rather than being carried by a prolonged successful defence
The governor cannot sustain the defence: Saturn, lord of the 4th for the governor, in his fall shows him weak, fallen and incapacitated in authority
Effective relief from the King will not arrive in time to raise the siege: the Sun, the King's significator, in the 7th in a fixed sign does not overcome the besieger
The delivery is near, on a days-scale within the present siege (by late April), as the Moon, though void of course, applies to Mars, significator of Essex, with reception
Essex gains honour from the taking despite hardship to his side: Mars is in his fall, but he is fortified by reception with the Moon in the 10th near Regulus
summary: Essex will take Reading shortly, by the town's surrender, the fallen governor being unable to hold it and the King unable to relieve it in time.
reasoning: Asc Scorpio: Mars = Essex, well fortified except in fall, mitigated by mutual reception with Moon in 10th near Regulus = honour and perfection via Moon applying to Mars (sextile equivalent to square in long ascension). 4th Aquarius = town; Saturn lord of 4th in fall = governor/town weak and fallen. Sun, King's significator, fixed in 7th gives no timely effective relief. Jupiter/Venus for provisions do not outweigh the 4th lord's fall, so provisions cannot sustain a long defence.
